newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close up on last minute buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close up on last minute buying.

text.p: Bargain hunters bought large capitalised communication and finance counters in a last minute reversal on Wednesday, driving the index which was in negative territory up slightly at the close, brokers said.

"Investors focused their attention today on the monthly key economic data to be released by the central bank tomorrow. They're also waiting for remarks to be given by US Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan later today," said a broker at Securities One.
The SET composite index, which moved in negative territory, rose 0.07 point to 739.82 on 3.6 billion baht turnover.
The SET-50 index posted a gain of 0.05 point to 54.78.
Decliners led gainers 162 to 147 while 88 issues were unchanged.
Brokers said economic figures released by the finance ministry soon after the market reopened in the afternoon did not have an impact on the market.

"I think the current account deficit figures in December were still unimpressive although it fell a bit," said Bunsom Kesapradist of Asia Credit, referring to the ministry's data which showed the current account deficit declined to 19.1 billion baht in December from 21.7 billion in November.
A broker at Securities One said although investors were waiting for Greenspan's remarks the issue may not be that significant for the Thai bourse as local issues were in focus.
Greenspan is scheduled to appear before the Senate Banking Committee later on Wednesday to give his semiannual testimony on the state of monetary policy and the economy.
His comments in last December caused financial markets around the world to tumble.
National Finance topped the active list, rising 1.25 baht to 37, Siam Cement retreated four to 712.
